Future Perfect for Predicting and Reporting Events
You use the Future Perfect tense to predict and report about future events.

You often use the phrase by the time to refer to a time that will happen before another time in the future.

For example:

I believe that Lincoln will have taught us a lot by the time the project finishes.

The structure of the Future Perfect is:

Subject + will + have + past participle

We hope that Lincoln will have left a positive, lasting impression.
It is our hope that with Lincoln's assistance over the next couple months, the next phase in our reinvention will have finished before Christmas.
Also, we hope that Lincoln will have left a positive, lasting impression.
We hope that you will have organized your schedules by then so everyone can meet him.
I believe that Lincoln will have taught us a lot by the time the project finishes.
He asked if Lincoln will have finished his other projects before he starts this new position?
Future Continuous: An Action That Will be in Progress Some Time in the Future
There are many ways to talk about the future. You can use the Future Continuous to talk about an action that will be in progress at some time in the future.

For example:

Don't call too early because I will be putting the baby to sleep.

The structure subject + will + be + v-ing refers to an action that will be happening at a time in the future or during a period in the future.

For example:

We'll be working on this project until the end of 2020.

images.text:
August 24th

Dear Staff:

Thank you for recently welcoming Adam and Kristi into the company. In addition, Lincoln Green has accepted our offer of employment as Director of Advertising Design. We believe that his appointment will have a lasting impact.
Please join us on Tuesday at 4 p.m. in the conference room for appetizers and drinks. We hope that you will have organized your schedules by then so everyone can meet him.

During the last 10 years, Lincoln has devoted himself to his work and education. From early on, Lincoln has had increasingly responsible roles in design layouts for high-quality magazine features, online publishing and social media sites.
Since June, Lincoln has been Director of Design for Fairjax Publishing, a global company with offices in London, Singapore and New York. He comes to us with a desire to drive our editorial vision, and provide a new engagement strategy.
His Bachelor's degree in Communication Design has provided a solid foundation for growth in the industry . Since then, he has also completed his MBA with a major in management. Recently, he has accepted a spot in the revered Master in Publishing program offered at Toronto University. Furthermore, he has been a full member of the Canadian Institute of Graphic Design with a COMD designation since 2009.

Lincoln will be leading our efforts in a number of areas. He will be performing professional work related to the overall management of design staff over the next ten months. From this point onward, he will also be acting as a liaison with the team to ensure that work is completed on time. Finally, he will be sharing his technical knowledge and personal experiences during monthly meeting that begin in two weeks.
It is our hope that the next phase in our reinvention will have finished before Christmas. Also, we hope that Lincoln will have left a positive, lasting impression.
Thanks for joining me in welcoming Lincoln to the team.

Regards,

Denise Moore, CEO

Imagine you have to send out a memo to the staff at your company. There is a new employee starting next week. What will be his role in the future?

The Future Continuous tense is used when an action will be in progress some time in the future.
Examples:
He will be performing professional work related to the overall management of editorial staff over the next ten months.
The next phase in our reinvention will have finished before Christmas.
With assistance from our design team, Lincoln will be creating a new look and feel for our magazine.
From this point onward, he will also be acting as a liaison with the team to ensure that work is completed on time.
